headline: 7 Bangladeshis killed in Kolkata hotel fire
summary: Two more victims from Satkhira have been identified, bringing the total number of confirmed Bangladeshi deaths to seven.
details: A devastating fire at Hotel Shikha Inn in Kolkata, India, has claimed the lives of seven Bangladeshi nationals.
The latest victims identified are Alimuzzaman Saju, 48, and Rebati Sarkar, 35, both residents of Kaliganj, Satkhira. Both had traveled to India for medical treatment.

Among the other deceased are four members of a single family from Kushtia: Debashish Dutta, 39; his wife, Afsana Sharmin, 27; their three-year-old son, Swarnashish Dutta; and father-in-law, Akram Ali, 60.
Another victim has been identified as 37-year-old Ahmed Babu from Savar, Dhaka.
The Bangladesh Deputy High Commission in Kolkata has opened a helpline (91 8274821352) to provide assistance to families and affected individuals.
caption:

Among the other deceased are four members of a single family from Kushtia: Debashish Dutta, 39; his wife, Afsana Sharmin, 27; their three-year-old son, Swarnashish Dutta; and father-in-law, Akram Ali, 60.

Another victim has been identified as 37-year-old Ahmed Babu from Savar, Dhaka.

The Bangladesh Deputy High Commission in Kolkata has opened a helpline (91 8274821352) to provide assistance to families and affected individuals.

headline: JS votes today to elect the 23rd president of Bangladesh
summary: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is set to be elected as the new president after 35 years of direct voting process.
details: The Jatiya Sangsad (JS) is voting today to elect the 23rd president of Bangladesh, marking a return to direct voting for the presidency after 35 years.
BNP nominee Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, who currently serves as the party's secretary general and LGRD minister, is expected to be elected.
Following the resignation of the 22nd president, Mohammed Shahabuddin, on July 24, the election was scheduled for August 20.
The law ministry has clarified that Barrister Kayser Kamal, acting as the Speaker, is the constitutionally appropriate authority to administer the oath of office to the new president.
The swearing-in ceremony is scheduled for 7:30 PM on Friday at the Darbar Hall of Bangabhaban.
The event will be attended by top state and government dignitaries, including the acting president, prime minister, and Chief Justice.
caption:
Bangladesh elects its 23rd president today after a 35-year gap in direct voting.

The Jatiya Sangsad (JS) is voting today to elect the 23rd president of Bangladesh, marking a return to direct voting for the presidency after 35 years.

BNP nominee Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, who currently serves as the party's secretary general and LGRD minister, is expected to be elected.

Following the resignation of the 22nd president, Mohammed Shahabuddin, on July 24, the election was scheduled for August 20.

The law ministry has clarified that Barrister Kayser Kamal, acting as the Speaker, is the constitutionally appropriate authority to administer the oath of office to the new president.

The swearing-in ceremony is scheduled for 7:30 PM on Friday at the Darbar Hall of Bangabhaban.

The event will be attended by top state and government dignitaries, including the acting president, prime minister, and Chief Justice.
